purpose: Test the direct parity-native Pfaffian/matchgate route for the occurrence tensor network under one common invertible 2x2 holographic basis.

tensor_network.clause_signature: For a positive 3-clause, f_OR=[0,1,1,1] in symmetric Hamming-weight notation; signed clauses differ by input bit flips.
tensor_network.variable_signature: An original variable of occurrence degree d contributes EQ_d=e0^(tensor d)+e1^(tensor d).
tensor_network.universal_test_family: A universal common-basis route must in particular handle instances containing both degree-3 and degree-4 equality vertices together with OR3 clause vertices.

source_fact.statement: Every matchgate signature satisfies a parity condition: its support lies entirely on even Hamming weight or entirely on odd Hamming weight. For symmetric signatures this is explicit in the standard matchgate classification.
source_fact.source: Cai, Fu, Guo, Williams, FKT is Not Universal — A Planar Holant Dichotomy for Symmetric Constraints, Theory of Computing Systems 66 (2022), Proposition 2.8 and surrounding matchgate discussion.

theorem.name: NO_COMMON_INVERTIBLE_BASIS_MAKES_EQ3_EQ4_AND_OR3_ALL_MATCHGATE_V1_2
theorem.statement: Over C (hence over characteristic zero), there is no single invertible 2x2 basis S such that S^(tensor 3) EQ_3 and S^(tensor 4) EQ_4 are matchgate signatures while the dual transformed clause (S^(-T))^(tensor 3) f_OR is also a matchgate signature.
proof: Write S=[[a,c],[b,d]], with columns u=(a,b)^T and v=(c,d)^T. Then S^(tensor k) EQ_k=u^(tensor k)+v^(tensor k).
If transformed EQ_3 is even-parity, its odd-weight entries give a^2 b+c^2 d=0 and b^3+d^3=0. If it is odd-parity, its even-weight entries give a^3+c^3=0 and a b^2+c d^2=0.
If transformed EQ_4 is even-parity, its odd-weight entries give a^3 b+c^3 d=0 and a b^3+c d^3=0. If it is odd-parity, its even-weight entries include a^4+c^4=0, a^2 b^2+c^2 d^2=0 and b^4+d^4=0.
Invertibility plus either EQ_3 parity case forces a,b,c,d all nonzero, so set r=c/a and s=d/b.
EQ3-even plus EQ4-even gives r^2 s=-1 and r^3 s=-1, hence r=1 and then s=-1.
EQ3-odd plus EQ4-even gives r^3=-1, r s^2=-1 and r^3 s=-1, hence s=1 and r=-1.
EQ3-even plus EQ4-odd gives r^2 s=-1 and r^2 s^2=-1, hence s=1; then r^2=-1, contradicting r^4=-1 from the EQ4 odd weight-zero condition.
EQ3-odd plus EQ4-odd gives r s^2=-1 and r^2 s^2=-1, hence r=1, contradicting r^3=-1.
Therefore, up to nonzero row scalings and harmless sign/column variants, S is Hadamard-type: [[a,a],[b,-b]] or [[a,-a],[b,b]].

For the first form, S^(-T)=diag(alpha,beta) H with alpha=1/(2a), beta=1/(2b). The unnormalized Hadamard transform of OR3 is 7 at mask 000 and -1 at every nonzero mask, so the transformed symmetric clause entries are [7 alpha^3, -alpha^2 beta, -alpha beta^2, -beta^3], all nonzero.
The second forced basis form only permutes/signs the same nonzero Fourier values, so again every Hamming-weight layer is nonzero.
Thus the transformed OR3 clause has support on both even and odd Hamming weights, violating the necessary matchgate parity condition. Contradiction.

algorithmic_consequence.killed: The direct plan: choose one common 2x2 holographic basis, turn all degree-3/degree-4 equality vertices and OR3 clause vertices into matchgates, then contract by a standard Pfaffian/FKT mechanism.
not_killed: edge-dependent or gadget-dependent basis changes outside the frozen common-basis model
nonlocal Pfaffian constructions that do not factor into local clause/equality matchgates
decision-only mechanisms that do not compute the #SAT contraction

next_target.name: E8_NONLOCAL_PARITY_CANCELLATION_OR_DECISION_ONLY_CORE_V1_3
next_target.directive: Stop retrying common-basis local matchgate conversion. Either construct a genuinely nonlocal parity-cancellation object whose size is polynomial, or switch from exact #SAT summation to a decision-only invariant and prove SAT iff nonzero without hidden exponential state.
success_obligations: no reliance on planarity or exponential crossover expansion
